title: The $L^2$-weight is at most the weight
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, the coefficient field $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ as in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $X_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve over $k_0$ (with the curve conventions of [sk-d-real-setup]). Let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil $\Qlb$-sheaf of rank $r$ on $X_0$ as in [sk-d-real-weil], punctually $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w\in\mathbf R$ in the sense of [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Then the $L^2$-weight parameter of [def-wf-l2-norm] satisfies
$$\|\mathcal F\|\le w.$$

proof.text: Fix a closed point $x$ of degree $e\ge1$ and put $q_x=q^e$. Take the finite mixed filtration $0=\mathcal F_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathcal F_s=\mathcal F$ with pure quotients of weights $w_i\le w$, supplied by [def-weil-punctual-weights]. By [lem-wf-rational-stalk-exact], its stalk at $\bar x$ is a filtration by Frobenius-stable subspaces, whose successive quotients are the stalks of those sheaf quotients. At each stage [lem-a1-spectrum-exact-sequence] says that the eigenvalue multiset is the union of the preceding subspace's and quotient's spectra. Starting with the zero subspace and repeating this for $i=1,\ldots,s$ shows that every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F_x$ occurs in a pure quotient. Thus $|\iota\alpha|=q_x^{w_i/2}\le q_x^{w/2}=q^{ew/2}$. Here $q_x>1$ and $w_i\le w$ give the inequality, without requiring $w\ge0$. The zero sheaf has empty eigenvalue multiset, so the assertion also covers $r=0$.

source.place: Proof, opening sentence: justify the punctual upper eigenvalue bound for a mixed filtration

proof.text: Fix $m\ge1$ and $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, lying over a closed point $x$ of degree $e$. The residue-field embedding $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow\mathbf F_{q^m}$ makes $e\mid m$ by the tower law, so $h=m/e\ge1$. Choose the finite coefficient field $E$ and lisse $E$-model supplied by [sk-d-real-weil], with its Weil pair interpreted in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], the same raw rationalized coefficient category as the local-power lemma. After enlarging $E$, [p-real-integral], applied with $U_0=C_0=X_0$, realizes a geometric lattice as a lisse $\mathcal O_E$-sheaf on $X$. Its reductions are finite locally constant free $\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$-modules in degree zero. Hence they are bounded constructible with Tor amplitude zero. Its rationalization is the chosen lisse $E$-model, so it supplies the integral representative required by [lem-trf-rational-local-frobenius-powers]; only the underlying lattice is used, and the Weil map need only be invertible after rationalization. That lemma gives $F_y^{(m)}=T^{-1}F_x^hT$ on the stalk, for an $E$-linear isomorphism $T$. Extending scalars to $\Qlb$ preserves this equality, by applying the same scalar extension to both sides. Consequently the trace at $y$ is $\operatorname{Tr}(F_x^h)$: in matrices, $\operatorname{Tr}(T^{-1}BT)=\operatorname{Tr}(BTT^{-1})=\operatorname{Tr}(B)$, since $\sum_{ij}a_{ij}b_{ji}=\sum_{ji}b_{ji}a_{ij}$.

source.place: Proof, opening sentence: rational-point Frobenius is the appropriate power of closed-point Frobenius

proof.text:
Enumerate the roots of the characteristic polynomial of $F_x$ as $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r$, with algebraic multiplicities. By [lem-wf-trace-power-eigenvalues] and the preceding two steps, the realized trace at $y$ is $\sum_{j=1}^r(\iota\alpha_j)^h$. The triangle inequality and multiplicativity of absolute value give
$$|\iota\operatorname{Tr}(F_y^{(m)})|\le\sum_{j=1}^r|\iota\alpha_j|^h\le r\,(q^{ew/2})^h=rq^{mw/2}.$$
Squaring gives $|\iota\operatorname{Tr}(F_y^{(m)})|^2\le r^2q^{mw}$. This also gives zero when $r=0$, and does not assume that Frobenius is semisimple.

source.place: Proof, first inequality: bound each squared trace by the rank squared times the punctual bound

proof.text:
By [lem-wf-point-count-linear-growth], choose $d\ge1$, independent of $m$, such that $\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})\le dq^m$ for every $m\ge1$; its hypotheses hold because $X_0$ is a smooth affine curve of finite type. The energy $S_m=\|f_{\mathcal F}\|_m^2$ in [def-wf-l2-norm] is a finite sum of the squared traces just bounded. Summing gives
$$0\le S_m\le r^2\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})q^{mw}\le dr^2q^{m(w+1)}.$$
Set $C=dr^2\ge0$. Empty rational-point sets contribute the empty sum $0$; the same $C$ works for all $m$.

source.place: Proof, second inequality: sum over rational points and use the uniform point-count bound

proof.text:
Let $\beta>w$ and set $b=q^{w-\beta}$. Positive real powers [def-weil-real-power] give $0<b<1$ since $q>1$ and $w-\beta<0$. Dividing the preceding bound by the positive denominator gives, for every $m\ge1$,
$$0\le\frac{S_m}{q^{m(\beta+1)}}\le Cq^{m(w-\beta)}=Cb^m.$$

source.place: Proof, last sentence: rewrite the normalized energy bound as geometric decay

proof.text: Apply [lem-wf-geometric-decay] to $b$ from step 5. For $C>0$ and any $\varepsilon>0$, eventually $b^m<\varepsilon/C$, whence $0\le S_m/q^{m(\beta+1)}<\varepsilon$. If $C=0$, all these ratios vanish for $m\ge1$. Thus the ratios tend to zero. In particular, their $\limsup$ is zero: every positive $\varepsilon$ eventually bounds the whole tail, while zero bounds every term below. The same argument computes the extended-nonnegative-real $\limsup$ used by the Lean definition; finite initial indices do not affect it.

source.place: Proof, last sentence: the limsup vanishes for every beta strictly greater than w

proof.text: Let $A=\{\beta\in\mathbf R:\limsup_m S_m/q^{m(\beta+1)}>0\}$, the set defining $\|\mathcal F\|$ in [def-wf-l2-norm]. Step 6 excludes every $\beta>w$ from $A$, so $w$ is an upper bound of $A$. Its supremum in the extended real numbers is therefore at most $w$. If $A$ is empty this is the stipulated value $-\infty\le w$, covering in particular the zero sheaf.

source.place: Proof, final conclusion: take the supremum of the positive-limsup exponents

proof_origin.place: Proof, expanded with explicit stalk exactness, Frobenius power comparison, trace power sums and geometric decay

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve over
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf of rank $r$
on $X_0$, punctually $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$.
Then

$$
\|\mathcal F\|\le w.
$$

proof.text:
At $y\in X_0(k_m)$ the eigenvalues of the Frobenius $F_y^{(m)}$
are the $m/d(y)$-th powers of the local eigenvalues at the closed
point below, hence have modulus at most $q^{mw/2}$ by the punctual
bounds of [def-weil-punctual-weights]; therefore

$$
\|f_{\mathcal F}\|_m^2\le r^2\cdot\#X_0(k_m)\cdot q^{mw}
\le C\,q^{m(w+1)}
$$

for a constant $C$ (the point-count bound of the affine curve,
[lem-wf-point-count-linear-growth] of the basic-weight chapter). The
$\limsup$ in [def-wf-l2-norm] is therefore $0$ for
$\beta>w$, hence $\|\mathcal F\|\le w$.
